newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil soyoil price rise reflects soybean exports.
newsitem.headline: Brazil soyoil price rise reflects soybean exports.

text.p: A sharp rise over the past few days in Brazilian soyoil export prices is due to the reduced availability of soyoil for export because of high soybean sales, traders said.
"It's simply that soybean exports are so high that industries are not crushing so much and this is being reflected in soyoil prices," one dealer said.
No traders had heard of any large-scale sales of soyoil abroad although most had heard of rumors last week that China may have been interested in buying Brazilian oil.
Soyoil prices have risen from a range of even to a 30 point discount (seller/buyer) to Chicago for June shipment at the end of last week to even to a 50 point premium today (buyer/seller).
"This year is not normal because it is the first without the ICMS tax. But I think prices will now start stabilising around these levels," one dealer said.
The lifting of ICMS taffifs, which favored export of products over soybeans, has led analysts to predict soybean exports of up to 8.5 million tonnes in 1997/98 (February/January).
Yesterday the Brazilian Vegetable Oils Industries Association (Abiove) reduced its crushing estimate by 500,000 tonnes to 18 million tonnes.

Soymeal exports it now sees at 8.9 million tonnes against a previous forecast of 9.3 million while soyoil exports are only expected to reach 850,000 tonnes against an April estimate of 950,000 tonnes.
